source_target_content: Achieve an annual production of sustainable biomethane of 35 billion cubic meters by 2030
impact_target_content: Improve air quality to reduce the number of premature deaths caused by air pollution by 55% by 2030
justification: The improvement of air quality can be reinforced by the production of sustainable biomethane, which can be used as a low-carbon fuel, thus reducing emissions from transportation and industry.

source_target_content: Aviation fuel suppliers shall also ensure that Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) made available to aircraft operators at each Union airport will be at least 2% from 2025, 6% from 2030, 20% from 2035, 34% from 2040, 42% from 2045 and 70% from 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/2405
impact_target_content: The Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) aims at preventing or reducing emissions from large industrial installations and intensive farming into the environment.
justification: The IED can support the development of SAF by reducing emissions from industrial installations, thus creating a more favorable environment for the production and use of SAF.

source_target_content: The share of biofuels and biogas produced from the feedstock listed in Part B of Annex IX in the energy content of fuels and electricity supplied to the transport sector shall, except in Cyprus and Malta, be limited to 1.7%. Directive (EU) 2023/2413
impact_target_content: Reduce by 25% the EU ecosystems where air pollution threatens biodiversity, by 2030
justification: The reduction of air pollution threatening biodiversity can be constrained by the limited share of biofuels and biogas from Part B of Annex IX, which may lead to increased emissions from other sources.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, at the end of each year, the following power output targets are met cumulatively: (a) for each light-duty battery electric vehicle registered in their territory, a total power output of at least 1.3 kW is provided through publicly accessible recharging stations, and (b) for each light-duty plug-in hybrid vehicle registered in their territory, a total power output of at least 0.80 kW is provided through publicly accessible recharging stations. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Improve soil quality by reducing chemical pesticides‚ use by 50%, by 2030
justification: The reduction of chemical pesticides can be enabled by the increased use of electric vehicles, which can reduce the need for pesticides in agricultural practices.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2030, at least one publicly accessible hydrogen refuelling station is deployed in each urban node. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Improve soil quality by reducing nutrient losses use by 50%, by 2030
justification: The reduction of nutrient losses can be supported by the development of hydrogen refuelling stations, which can promote the use of low-carbon fuels in transportation.

source_target_content: Member States shall ensure that at least one installation providing shore-side electricity supply to inland waterway vessels is deployed at all TEN-T core inland waterway ports by 1 January 2025, at least one installation providing shore-side electricity supply to inland waterway vessels is deployed at all TEN-T comprehensive inland waterway ports by 1 January 2030. Regulation (EU) 2023/1804
impact_target_content: Having all soils in healthy condition by 2050
justification: The goal of having all soils in healthy condition can be reinforced by the development of shore-side electricity supply for inland waterway vessels, which can reduce emissions from waterway transport.

source_target_content: EU fisheries are encouraged to continue the positive trend, as observed for the period 2009-2019, towards reducing fuel intensity by reducing the fossil-fuel consumption per kg of landed product for at least an additional 15% for the period 2019-2030. Energy Transition of the EU Fisheries and Aquaculture sector
impact_target_content: The revised Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (UWWTD) extends the scope of the 1991 UWWTD
justification: The revised UWWTD can support the energy transition in the fisheries and aquaculture sector by reducing emissions from wastewater treatment, thus creating a more favorable environment for the reduction of fuel intensity.

source_target_content: Of the SAF targets reported above, synthetic aviation fuels should represent a minimum share of 1.2% from 2030, 5% from 2035, 10% from 2034, 15% from 2045, and 35% from 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/2405
impact_target_content: Improve water quality by reducing waste, plastic litter at sea (by 50%)
justification: The reduction of waste and plastic litter at sea can be constrained by the increased use of synthetic aviation fuels, which may lead to increased emissions from aviation.

source_target_content: In the first phase, from 2020 up to 2024, the strategic objective is to install at least 6 GW of renewable hydrogen electrolysers in the EU. In the second phase, from 2025 up to 2030, the strategic objective is to install at least 40 GW of renewable hydrogen electrolysers. A Hydrogen Strategy for a climate-neutral Europe
impact_target_content: Improve water quality by reducing microplastics released into the environment (by 30%)
justification: The reduction of microplastics can be supported by the development of renewable hydrogen electrolysers, which can reduce emissions from industrial processes and promote the use of low-carbon fuels.

source_target_content: The yearly average GHG intensity of the energy used on board by a ship during a reporting period shall be reduced, compared to the reference value (91.16 gCO2e/MJ) by: 2% from 1 January 2025, 6% from 1 January 2030, 14.5% from 1 January 2035, 31% from 1 January 2040, 62% from 1 January 2045, 80% from 1 January 2050. Regulation (EU) 2023/1805
impact_target_content: By means of an updated and harmonised list of pollutants affecting surface and groundwater, updated existing quality standards, new monitoring requirements, improved and more accessible data, and a more flexible framework for addressing pollutants of emerging concerns
justification: The updated list of pollutants and quality standards can support the reduction of GHG emissions from shipping by promoting the use of low-carbon fuels and reducing emissions from industrial processes.

source_target_content: Cut the emissions of transport sector by 90% by 2050 relative to 1990. Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy
impact_target_content: Reduce the share of people chronically disturbed by transport noise by 30%, by 2030
justification: The reduction of transport noise can be supported by the development of low-carbon fuels and the reduction of emissions from the transport sector, thus creating a more favorable environment for the reduction of noise pollution.

source_target_content: Zero-emission in urban logistics The new EU Urban Mobility Framework
impact_target_content: Improve soil quality by reducing chemical pesticides‚ use by 50%, by 2030
justification: The reduction of chemical pesticides can be enabled by the development of zero-emission logistics, which can reduce the need for pesticides in agricultural practices and promote the use of low-carbon fuels in transportation.
